title: Frontend: Power of Four
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Power of Four. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(n), true only for safe positive integer powers of four, including one. Do not rely on 32-bit masks.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Repeatedly divide a validated positive integer by four while divisible and accept only when the final value is one.
alternativeApproaches: Return the base-four exponent and test values beyond the signed 32-bit range.
commonMistakes: Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
